text:
oliver: @channel AcmeCorp reporting p99 spikes ~700-1200ms on /v1/generate for EU users starting ~10:20 UTC. They supplied trace id 8a3f2c. Observed traces show a us-central1 smart-router hop between eu edge and model-serving — shouldn't happen for EU-origin traffic.
maya: Share the trace and any headers they captured. Also which SDK + runtime?
oliver: SDK acme-sdk/2.4.1. Trace 8a3f2c (from our tracer):
```
span0 edge-proxy eu-west1 10:20:12.003 -> root
span1 smart-router us-central1 10:20:12.105 (added ~102ms)
span2 model-router eu-west1 10:20:12.210 (added ~105ms)
span3 model-serving eu-west1 10:20:12.350 (added ~140ms)
```
Aggregate added latency ~350ms; customer sees 700-1200ms due to TLS and queuing. They included a tcpdump sample showing SYN->ACK RTT ~260ms for flows hitting 198.51.100.12 (us-central1).
```
10:20:12.100 IP 198.51.100.12.443 > 203.0.113.55.52344: Flags [P.], seq 1:501, ack 1, win 65535, length 500
RTT approx 260ms observed on SYN->ACK for some affected flows
```
jing: smart-router in us-central1 on an EU-origin path is unexpected. Which routing policy applied (region_preference, tenant priority)?
oliver: No region hints from client. Sample request headers they sent:
```
x-request-id: acme-req-104
user-agent: acme-sdk/2.4.1
```
luis: I'm looking at control plane events around 10:15-10:25. There's a transient autoscaler shift at 10:17 that temporarily routed overflow to a cheaper burst pool in us-central1. A guardrail that should block cross-region fallbacks for tenants with tenant_priority=high failed briefly (see INF-482). Hypothesis: when eu-west1 reserved pool saturated, smart-router incorrectly fell back cross-region.
tracebot: Automated correlation -> 57 traces from various EU-origin tenants between 10:17:30 and 10:21:20 show the same cross-hop pattern. Also flagged peering AS-path change via us-central1 for ~3.5 minutes.
maya: AcmeCorp flagged as P1. Account team wants immediate ETA for mitigation and customer-facing workaround.
oliver: Repro test: forcing header X-Region-Hint: eu-west1 from EU test node reduces p99 to ~120ms; without header p99 ~900ms. So pinning works as temporary mitigation.
jing: Forensics checklist: - validate smart-router weight/fallback config at 10:15-10:25; - confirm autoscaler state and reserved pool health; - review commit/rollback history for INF-482 guardrail; - request backbone/peering logs for AS-path change window.
luis: I'm preparing a hotfix to re-add the guardrail check. Pushing INF-482-fix as a canary to eu-west1 routers at 10:30. Canary monitor: rollback if smart-route-cross-region > 0.5%. Deploy log:
```
deploy hotfix INF-482-fix -> canary eu-west1
monitoring rule: smart-route-cross-region > 0.5% -> rollback
```
maya: Told customer about header workaround (X-Region-Hint) and that we're patching routing. Also opened billing hold for the 10:17-10:22 window pending SLA credit.
oliver: AcmeCorp accepted header workaround; asks about cost impact — explained that pinning may increase cost in burst scenarios but reduces latency.
tracebot: Canary metrics at 10:34: 34/34 canary requests stayed within EU, no cross hops observed; p99 ~110ms.
luis: Hotfix promoted at 10:36 to all eu-west1 routers after canary passed. Rolling deploy continuing.
jing: Post-deploy checks: sample traces after promotion show no us-central1 spans, SYN RTTs normal (~20ms). Log grep for "fallback-to-us-central" shows entries only in 10:17-10:22 window.
maya: Customer confirmation: "latency normalized, thanks. We'll keep monitoring." They requested a postmortem and timeline.
oliver: I'll draft the postmortem with timeline, root cause (INF-482 guardrail race), immediate mitigation (region hint header + hotfix), and long-term actions.
account-team-bot: SLA credit flagged for AcmeCorp for 10:17-10:22 UTC. Owner: maya.
maya: Actions added to incident board: 1) add unit tests for fallback policy; 2) run synthetic EU load tests exercising reserved pool; 3) improve tracer span tagging to include routing-decision metadata.
oliver: Posting postmortem link when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
